correctness.rationale: The Bernoulli flip likelihood of the exact two-state CTMC gives independent per-gap Fisher terms. f has a unique positive maximum and derivative f'(0)=1 strictly larger than every positive-gap derivative, guaranteeing interior maximizers. Strict concavity near zero gives the short-horizon equal-spacing law. For a fixed number of gaps and unbounded horizon, comparison with m-1 individually optimal gaps forces exactly one diverging component, all others tending to a; local injectivity of f' then establishes equality of all short gaps and a unique high-horizon scalar root. Taylor expansion at a and the exponential long-gap tail give the exact asymptotic short-gap correction and exponential information ratio. An exact rational-polynomial factorization plus e^2>7 validates the finite counterexample. Standalone code reproduces the Fisher identity, rational factorization, finite path enumeration and asymptotic numerical instances, but infinite claims depend on written proof.

originality.rationale: The published symmetric-CTMC optimal periodic interval, general Markov Fisher additivity, and qualitative nonuniform schedules are credited as prior art. The candidate statement is instead the all-fixed-observation-count global optimality classification under compulsory end-of-deployment observation, including the uniquely displaced short gaps, sharp exponential correction, and exponentially large information ratio. A substantive search did not establish that this all-budget, long-forced-horizon theorem follows from inspected published claims; historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A 2013 follow-up by Pagendam and Ross is potentially relevant but its complete text could not be read through available authorized access.
Another historical optimal-design source may contain an equivalent large-fixed-terminal-horizon specialization under a different vocabulary.
The proposed theorem is a locally optimal two-state model with perfect observation; it does not cover richer migration telemetry or unknown-rate robust designs.
Same-model review is not independent validation.

value.rationale: Compulsory starting and terminal GPS fixes under fixed battery observation budget make the sum-of-gaps constraint natural, and increasing deployment horizon creates a fundamentally different information-design regime. The precise all-budget optimal structure and the quantified exponential loss of equally spaced fixes identify a nontrivial, actionable mathematical boundary, beyond the known best unconstrained single period and known qualitative nonuniformity. The result is a rigorous benchmark for ecological telemetry, not an empirical scheduling recommendation.
